license.verdict: MIT — CONCLUSIVELY ESTABLISHED. Licensing is NOT unresolved and NOT genuinely ambiguous; no unresolved item remains and no policy waiver was required or invoked.
license.upstream_prose: v4.0 README line 62: 'Published under permissive license (MIT) Silero VAD has zero strings attached - no telemetry, no keys, no registration, no built-in expiration, no keys or vendor lock.'
license.separate_model_license_file_at_v4_tag: NONE — `git ls-tree -r v4.0` yields LICENSE as the only licence-named file in the entire tree; files/ contains no licence file. The R1-BLOCKER-DECISION-PACKET parenthetical that 'upstream ships a separate licence for the model' is NOT substantiated for the v4 VAD artifact.
resolution_evidence: LICENSE at tag v4.0 is MIT, sha256 2e63e9a38b6e8fc0c7bc37ce174caca1862870856c6daf5697cfb785e925520b, byte-identical to the shipped SILERO_VAD_LICENSE_MIT.txt.

The repository was NEVER relicensed: `git log --all -- LICENSE` returns exactly one commit (caddb3b7 'Add License', 2020-11-23). No commit in the repository's history changed the licence to or from CC BY-NC.

The alt-text is a demonstrable relicensing leftover: at caddb3b7 — the same commit that introduced MIT — the badge was [![License: CC BY-NC 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GNU%20AGPL%203.0-lightgrey.svg)](https://github.com/snakers4/silero-models/blob/master/LICENSE). Alt-text said CC BY-NC 4.0, the badge IMAGE said GNU AGPL 3.0, and the LINK pointed at a different repository. Only the image and link were later corrected to MIT / silero-vad; the alt-text string was never updated. Three mutually inconsistent licence strings in one badge proves the alt-text is stale boilerplate, not a grant.

'CC BY-NC' occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the entire v4.0 tree, at README.md:1, and only inside the [![...]] alt-text attribute (git grep -i -E 'cc[ -]?by|by-nc|noncommercial' v4.0). No CC BY-NC licence file, no licence header in any source file. Alt-text is presentational accessibility metadata with no grant effect.
The badge's machine-readable channels say MIT: image URL img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-lightgrey.svg, link target = the MIT LICENSE file.
license.known_upstream_metadata_anomaly: RESOLVED (was previously disclosed as an unresolved badge mismatch). The upstream README badge alt-text reads 'License: CC BY-NC 4.0' while the badge image reads 'License: MIT' and links to the MIT LICENSE file. This is erroneous README badge alt-text — a stale relicensing leftover, NOT a licence statement, and NOT applicable to files/silero_vad.onnx. Determinant: the same commit that introduced the MIT LICENSE (caddb3b7) carried the CC BY-NC alt-text alongside a badge image still reading 'GNU AGPL 3.0' and a link to a different repository; the image and link were later corrected to MIT and the alt-text was never updated. CC BY-NC appears exactly once in the whole v4.0 tree, only as alt-text; the sole licence file at v4.0 is unambiguous MIT and unchanged across all three v4-era commits checked (081e6b98, 1baf307b, 915dd3d6, each sha256 2e63e9a3…). The anomaly remains disclosed here for owner/legal visibility and is NOT suppressed; it required no written determination because the licence is affirmatively established by primary evidence, not waived.
license.adjacent_noncommercial_reference_scope: README.md:92 at v4.0 links the snakers4/silero-models wiki 'Licensing and Tiers', whose CE tier is 'provided as-is under a non-commercial License'. That page governs the silero-models STT repository — a DIFFERENT upstream project and its model tiers — and does NOT apply to files/silero_vad.onnx from silero-vad. Separately, the other CC BY-NC hits on master are in datasets/README.md, a third-party TRAINING-DATASET catalogue (globalrecordings.net CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, VoxLingua107 CC BY 4.0, Common Voice CC0); no datasets/ directory exists at v4.0 and no dataset is bundled by this PR.

upstream_revision_integrity: CORRECTION to the earlier record, which described tag v4.0 as an 'immutable release tag'. It is not. v4.0 is an ANNOTATED tag created 2024-07-08 (tagger adamnsandle) whose message is literally 'moving tag to new commit', pointing at commit 915dd3d639b8333a52e001af095f87c5b7f1e0ac — not the 2022-10-28 release commit. This does not weaken the licence conclusion: the MIT LICENSE is byte-identical (sha256 2e63e9a3…) at 081e6b98 ('VAD v4', 2022-10-26), 1baf307b ('v4 hotfix', 2022-10-27) and 915dd3d6 (2024-07-08). It does mean the tag cannot be used as the sole pin, which is why identity is anchored on the content-addressed blob SHA-1. The pre-hotfix v4 commit 081e6b98 carries a DIFFERENT blob (ffbfbbabc0a92a36288da7ac9b2bb3e4b67f6403), so the hotfix blob e6db48d6… — not the first v4 build — is the correct v4 artifact.
